extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of political philosophy / classical literature; designers of civic education or utopian institutions
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and prescriptions for selecting, educating, housing, and regulating the guardian (ruling/warrior) class in an ideal city-state, emphasizing civic utility, moral character, and balanced training. Includes qualifications for related professions (judges, physicians) and institutional limits (property, state size, class mobility).

rubrics_metrics.name: Education chiefly aims to improve the soul
rubrics_metrics.description: Music and gymnastic are primarily for the improvement of the soul rather than merely for bodily training or technical skill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teachers of both music and gymnastics should direct their arts chiefly to the soul: music tempers and refines the spirited element, gymnastics stimulates spirit without turning it merely to brute strength. The balance of both is more important than extreme development of either.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance music and gymnastics to harmonize soul
rubrics_metrics.description: Proper education mixes music and gymnastic in fair proportions so that the spirited and philosophical elements are harmonized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excessive music produces softness and effeminacy; exclusive gymnastics produces hardness and ferocity. The true musician/harmonist knows how to attemper both so the soul is both gentle and courageous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guardians must be temperate, courageous, and harmonious
rubrics_metrics.description: Those chosen as rulers/guardians should possess a harmonious soul in which spirit and reason are in proper proportion, producing temperance and courage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A harmonious guardian is neither soft nor savage; education should cultivate gentleness tempered by spirit and spiritedness tempered by gentleness, so the guardian can both defend and govern wisely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select guardians who love the city and reject its harm
rubrics_metrics.description: Guardians should be chosen from those who show the greatest eagerness to do what is for the good of the country and the greatest repugnance to what is against its interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe candidates from youth upwards; prefer those whose actions and inclinations consistently align with the city's welfare rather than personal gain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lifelong surveillance and staged testing of guardians
rubrics_metrics.description: Guardians must be watched at every age and subjected to trials (toils, pains, conflicts, enchantments) to ensure they retain conviction and are not deceived or corrupted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tests should include trials by persuasion (argument), time (forgetting), force (pain/compulsion), and enchantment (pleasure/fear). Only those who remain steadfast at boyhood, youth, and maturity are appointed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use myths/education to bind citizens to the state
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundational tales (e.g., the 'noble lie' of metals) may be employed to foster unity, sense of common origin, and duty to the city.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The myth tells citizens they were 'born of the earth' and have different metals (gold, silver, brass/iron) mixed into their souls; it is used to make them care for the city and accept assigned roles, while allowing for occasional natural transposition of ranks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guardians must not hold private property or household wealth
rubrics_metrics.description: Guardians should have no private property beyond what is absolutely necessary: no private houses, private stores, or personal gold/silver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They should live communally like soldiers, receive a fixed rate of pay sufficient for the year, dine together, and refrain from touching or wearing gold or silver. This prevents them becoming housekeepers, husbands, or tyrants driven by private interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guardians' dwellings and lifestyle must prevent corruption
rubrics_metrics.description: Guardians' houses and all that belongs to them should be arranged so as neither to impair their virtue nor to tempt them to prey upon other citizens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Houses should be of soldiers not shopkeepers; arrangements must avoid hunger, want, or luxury that could make auxiliaries turn into tyrants or predators on the populace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain class roles for unity and functioning of the State
rubrics_metrics.description: Each person should be put to the use for which nature intended him — one to one work — so the city is 'one and self-sufficing' and each class receives its due proportion of happiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid making every class aspire to every good; the stability and justice of the state depend on individuals performing their natural function rather than seeking disproportionate private happiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote/demote offspring by nature, not by birth alone
rubrics_metrics.description: Children should be elevated or degraded into classes (guardians, auxiliaries, artisans) according to natural aptitude rather than strictly by parentage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the 'noble lie' emphasizes fixed metal-types, practical policy requires watching offspring and moving them up or down the scale when nature indicates, preserving the best for guardianship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guardians as the first concern: purity of the race and state safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Rulers must guard above all else the purity of the guardian class and be severe in ensuring only fit persons occupy these roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An oracle warns that if a man of brass or iron guards the State it will be destroyed; guardians must therefore be chosen and policed to prevent destructive elements entering their ranks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physicians' practice should serve the State's interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Medicine ought not to 'educate diseases' or prolong lives that are useless to the individual or to the State; it should treat definite ailments in persons otherwise fit to live their ordinary lives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asclepius' successors treat acute wounds and restore those with healthy habits; they decline to spend resources on valetudinarian arts that perpetuate weak, unproductive lives (Herodicus criticized for cultivating lingering death).

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications for physicians: combine technical knowledge with experience of disease
rubrics_metrics.description: The most skilful physicians are those who pair knowledge of their art with extensive experience of diseases — even personal familiarity with sickness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physicians cure with the mind; experience of illness enables understanding of disease varieties. The text suggests physicians need not be robust and may have themselves been sickly to better comprehend maladies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications for judges: avoid contamination by vice; prefer long observation
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges should not have been trained among vicious minds or themselves practised many crimes; they should know evil by observation in others and through mature reflection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A judge's honourable mind should be guided by knowledge, not by personal criminal experience. Preference is for older, wise men who have learned the nature of evil externally, not by having committed it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against degeneration of arts from wealth or poverty
rubrics_metrics.description: Both wealth and poverty corrupt crafts: wealth breeds indolence and deterioration; poverty prevents proper tools and teaching and likewise degrades workmanship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guardians must watch to prevent extremes of wealth or want which lead to decline in skills and moral worth across professions; distribution and institutional checks are necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit the size of the State to preserve unity and self-sufficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: The State should grow only so far as is consistent with unity; a measure of territory and population that preserves oneness and self-sufficing is preferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid imperial expansion that undermines unity; a well-ordered, moderate-sized State with disciplined guardians will be stronger in deed even if numerically small.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize the good of the whole over individual class happiness
rubrics_metrics.description: The design goal is maximum happiness for the whole city, not the disproportionate happiness of any single class; individual sacrifices (e.g., guardians' worldly pleasures) serve the common good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assigning roles and rewards, aim for the well-ordered State in which justice emerges and the collective happiness is the metric, rather than making each class individually as comfortable as possible.
